<div class="sd:space-y-4 sd:whitespace-normal sd:[&>*:first-child]:mt-0 sd:[&>*:last-child]:mb-0">

This is **ChrisFix**’s 2019 video *How to Rebuild the Entire Front Suspension in your Car or Truck* (about 23 minutes). It is **Part 1 of 2**: teardown and knuckle rebuild on an older high-mileage Honda. Installation is the follow-up video.<a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mQ2fJ_aM_T0" class="no-copy ms-1 inline text-nowrap print:hidden py-[2.5px] ps-2 pe-2 rounded-full align-[0.5px] bg-surface-l1 text-[13px] leading-none font-medium !text-fg-secondary hover:!text-fg-primary visited:text-fg-secondary focus:outline-none !no-underline hover:!no-underline citation" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer nofollow" data-state="closed">⁠YouTube</a>

He replaces essentially everything from the wheel inward on one front corner.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Suspension parts being replaced

**Main components**

- Lower control arm (including bushings)
- Upper control arm (including bushings and upper ball joint)
- Lower ball joint (pressed into the steering knuckle)
- Wheel hub
- Wheel bearing
- Inner tie rod
- Outer tie rod end
- Strut / strut assembly and strut fork
- Drive axle / CV axle (and boots)

**Hardware and related pieces**

- Bearing snap rings
- Ball-joint snap ring and boot
- Cotter pins and castle nuts
- Fasteners in general (he recommends new hardware, not reused rusty bolts)
- Dust shield (removed; often skipped on reassembly if rusted through)

**Temporarily removed (not “suspension,” but in the job)**

- Brake caliper, caliper bracket hardware, and rotor
- Brake-line clips / 10 mm fasteners

He also preps and paints the **knuckle**, **strut fork**, and **wheel-well / chassis** so the new parts go onto clean metal.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Tools used

**Common hand tools**

- Floor jack and jack stands
- Breaker bar
- Ratchets, sockets, and wrenches (he uses an extendable ratchet; sizes called out include 10 mm, 14 mm, 17 mm)
- Torque wrench (more critical on install)
- Pry bar
- Hammer (he lists a 4 lb hammer)
- Punch
- Pliers and snap-ring pliers
- Screwdrivers (flat and Phillips; he slots rusted Phillips screws so a flat blade will turn them)
- File
- 400-grit sandpaper
- Wire brush
- Vice

**Specialty tools (he says these can be rented)**

- Slide hammer (plus hub adapter; he improvises with lug nuts if needed)
- Ball-joint puller
- Ball-joint press
- Bearing / hub press and adapters

**Consumables / extras**

- Penetrating oil (soaked for days on rusty bolts)
- Impact gun (optional; listed in the description)
- Hose, soapy water, and a brush to degrease the wheel well
- Fan to dry parts
- Rust-bonding primer and thick black rust paint
- Safety glasses / gloves (standard shop practice)

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Outline of work steps

This video is **removal + knuckle prep**. Steps below follow the order he works, with parts and tools called out.

### 1. Diagnose and soak fasteners

- **Parts:** bushings, ball joints, bearing, tires
- **Tools:** pry bar
- Check play in control-arm bushings and ball joints; note cupping / inner-edge tire wear. Soak every suspension bolt with penetrating oil ahead of time.

### 2. Raise the car and pull the wheel

- **Tools:** jack, jack stands, lug wrench / impact
- Support the car securely. Remove the front wheel.

### 3. Remove the axle nut

- **Parts:** axle nut (staked / indented)
- **Tools:** punch, hammer, long breaker bar; screwdriver through rotor vanes or hold the brakes so the axle does not spin
- Unstake the nut, then break it loose.

### 4. Remove the brakes

- **Parts:** caliper, caliper bolts, brake-line clips, rotor
- **Tools:** sockets (10 mm on line clips), hammer
- Unbolt the caliper and hang it so the hose is not stretched. Hammer the rotor off if it is stuck.

### 5. Pull the hub off the knuckle

- **Parts:** hub
- **Tools:** slide hammer + adapter, or hammer if the slide hammer will not bite
- Hub often comes off the bearing face only after serious persuasion.

### 6. Separate the ball joints and tie rod from the knuckle

- **Parts:** upper ball joint, lower ball joint, outer tie rod, cotter pins, castle nuts
- **Tools:** pliers, hammer, ball-joint puller
- Typical ChrisFix trick: loosen the castle nut, flip it over on the stud so the threads are protected, then hammer the stud out of the taper. Use a puller if it will not pop.

### 7. Unbolt and remove the strut

- **Parts:** strut pinch bolt, lower strut-to-control-arm bolt, strut-tower nuts (14 mm), strut + fork
- **Tools:** wrenches, sockets, breaker bar, hammer to tap the pinch bolt
- Support the knuckle/arm so it does not drop. Lift the strut out of the tower.

### 8. Remove the axle from the transmission

- **Parts:** CV axle
- **Tools:** pry bar
- Pry the inner joint out of the transaxle. Catch dripping fluid.

### 9. Unbolt the control arms

- **Parts:** upper control arm (two nuts/bolts), lower control arm (bushing bolts + main 17 mm bolt)
- **Tools:** sockets, wrenches, breaker bar
- Once the knuckle is free, the arms come off the chassis.

### 10. Bench work: strip the knuckle

- **Parts:** remaining hub, wheel bearing, snap rings, dust shield, pressed-in lower ball joint
- **Tools:** hammer, sockets used as drifts, punch, screwdriver/pick, snap-ring pliers, penetrating oil, optionally bearing/ball-joint press
- Hammer the hub out. Soak and tap the bearing snap ring free, then drive the bearing out. Slot rusted dust-shield screws if needed. Remove the ball-joint snap ring and boot, then drive or press the ball joint out.

### 11. Clean and paint

- **Parts:** knuckle, strut fork, wheel well / chassis
- **Tools:** file, 400-grit paper, wire brush, hose + soap + brush, fan, rust-bonding primer, black rust paint
- File burrs, sand mating surfaces, degrease the well, dry, then paint so new parts are not sitting on rust.

At that point the corner is empty and the knuckle is ready for new bearing, ball joint, and hub. Those press-in and reassembly steps are in the next video: <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=V_g1-WHD4rw" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer nofollow">How to Install a COMPLETELY New Front Suspension</a>.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

**Practical notes from the video**

- This Honda uses a **pressed lower ball joint and pressed wheel bearing** in the knuckle; many other cars are similar, but fastener sizes and whether the upper joint is integral to the arm will differ.
- After a full rebuild he still sends the car for a **professional alignment**.
- Do not reuse old cotter pins, snap rings, or badly rusted fasteners.

If you want the same three lists written against **Part 2 (install + torque values)**, say so and I will map that video the same way.

What the file contains:

- Every populated vPIC field (identity, plant, engine, drive, GVWR, airbags, TPMS, brakes)
- VIN position breakdown
- Explicit list of empty vPIC fields so missing data is not read as “feature absent”
- 18 model-year recall campaigns, split into **likely 2.0 L-relevant**, **1.6 L-only (should not apply)**, and **short build-window**
- Pointer to run a *VIN-specific* open-recall check at <a href="https://www.nhtsa.gov/recalls" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer nofollow">nhtsa.gov/recalls</a> — the YMM list is not the same as “this VIN still has an open campaign”

Notable for this VIN: it is the **2.0**, not the 1.6 that carried the early overheat/fire recalls. Campaigns that still matter on a 2.0 Titanium include shifter-cable bushing (18S20 / 22S43), door latches, RCM/airbags, MAP-sensor wiring on early 2.0 builds, seatback welds, and the 2026 **2.0 block-heater** campaign (26S01) — do not plug in a block heater until that one is closed.

The official feed is **<span class="text-sm px-1 rounded-sm !font-mono bg-orange-400/10 text-orange-500 dark:bg-orange-300/10 dark:text-orange-300">@bot</span>** (display name Grok Bot), not the old <span class="text-sm px-1 rounded-sm !font-mono bg-orange-400/10 text-orange-500 dark:bg-orange-300/10 dark:text-orange-300">@GrokBot</span> account. The three day-long X broadcasts are the videos on that feed. **Day 1 — Building a company with Grok Bot** (research, plan, product; sessions: Grok Bot 101, Engineering, Product, Founders). Posted by <span class="text-sm px-1 rounded-sm !font-mono bg-orange-400/10 text-orange-500 dark:bg-orange-300/10 dark:text-orange-300">@bot</span> Tue Sep 15. ~8h 45m broadcast.

Broadcast: <a href="https://x.com/i/broadcasts/1AxRnZbVpjaxl" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer nofollow">x.com/i/broadcasts/1AxRnZbVpjaxl</a> · Announcement: <a href="https://x.com/bot/status/2099890276315848743" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer nofollow">x.com/bot/status/2099890276315848743</a>

<span class="text-sm px-1 rounded-sm !font-mono bg-orange-400/10 text-orange-500 dark:bg-orange-300/10 dark:text-orange-300">@Jdizzy_85</span>: asked if it would be watchable after the live window — “some people still have a 9-5.” <span class="text-sm px-1 rounded-sm !font-mono bg-orange-400/10 text-orange-500 dark:bg-orange-300/10 dark:text-orange-300">@kellyocornell</span>: “Watching on a projector.” <span class="text-sm px-1 rounded-sm !font-mono bg-orange-400/10 text-orange-500 dark:bg-orange-300/10 dark:text-orange-300">@AunySillyMe</span>: called Grok Bots her favorites and described running a group chat of specialist bots (Aperture / Vidness / Lyrically) to make a music video. <span class="text-sm px-1 rounded-sm !font-mono bg-orange-400/10 text-orange-500 dark:bg-orange-300/10 dark:text-orange-300">@kononovme</span>: “agents fail at permissions and sharing, not at the model… every extra bot roughly doubles token usage, so start with one bot, one job.” <span class="text-sm px-1 rounded-sm !font-mono bg-orange-400/10 text-orange-500 dark:bg-orange-300/10 dark:text-orange-300">@SawyerMerritt</span> circulated the Day 1 link early. <span class="text-sm px-1 rounded-sm !font-mono bg-orange-400/10 text-orange-500 dark:bg-orange-300/10 dark:text-orange-300">@Grok</span> later confirmed Day 1/2 replays stay up.

**Day 2 — Building a company with Grok Bot** (GTM + customer support sessions). Posted by <span class="text-sm px-1 rounded-sm !font-mono bg-orange-400/10 text-orange-500 dark:bg-orange-300/10 dark:text-orange-300">@bot</span> Wed Sep 16.

Broadcast: <a href="https://x.com/i/broadcasts/1PKqrNyvmYwGb" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer nofollow">x.com/i/broadcasts/1PKqrNyvmYwGb</a> · Announcement: <a href="https://x.com/bot/status/2100246135420199140" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer nofollow">x.com/bot/status/2100246135420199140</a>

<span class="text-sm px-1 rounded-sm !font-mono bg-orange-400/10 text-orange-500 dark:bg-orange-300/10 dark:text-orange-300">@DonaldMoor91672</span> (<span class="text-sm px-1 rounded-sm !font-mono bg-orange-400/10 text-orange-500 dark:bg-orange-300/10 dark:text-orange-300">GemHunterAI</span>): liked the build but asked for a “Grok Bot for Dummies” path — “I’m not technical… a plain-language starter would help a lot of people like me.” <span class="text-sm px-1 rounded-sm !font-mono bg-orange-400/10 text-orange-500 dark:bg-orange-300/10 dark:text-orange-300">@iYaT_TA</span>: “we don’t have unlimited tokens just like you guys. Btw how much did this demo cost by now?” View count on the announcement post ran into the millions; several people treated Day 2 as the commercial-workflow day (sales / support) rather than more coding.

**Day 3 — Building a company with Grok Bot** (marketing + customer success; final showcase / launch). Posted by <span class="text-sm px-1 rounded-sm !font-mono bg-orange-400/10 text-orange-500 dark:bg-orange-300/10 dark:text-orange-300">@bot</span> Thu Sep 17. Live at the time of this lookup.

Broadcast: <a href="https://x.com/i/broadcasts/1YGNrbXEeazGw" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer nofollow">x.com/i/broadcasts/1YGNrbXEeazGw</a> · Announcement: <a href="https://x.com/bot/status/2100609778917822704" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer nofollow">x.com/bot/status/2100609778917822704</a>

<span class="text-sm px-1 rounded-sm !font-mono bg-orange-400/10 text-orange-500 dark:bg-orange-300/10 dark:text-orange-300">@XFreeze</span>: “today they actually launch it… this is where the whole experiment comes together.” <span class="text-sm px-1 rounded-sm !font-mono bg-orange-400/10 text-orange-500 dark:bg-orange-300/10 dark:text-orange-300">@br_huni</span>: “we’ll need a 10–15 minute recap of what was done.” <span class="text-sm px-1 rounded-sm !font-mono bg-orange-400/10 text-orange-500 dark:bg-orange-300/10 dark:text-orange-300">@ShannaFaye39</span>: “so generous of @bot to share all of this live.” <span class="text-sm px-1 rounded-sm !font-mono bg-orange-400/10 text-orange-500 dark:bg-orange-300/10 dark:text-orange-300">@kaikihuang</span>: “Clay’s still in the sidebar like a coworker with better focus.” <span class="text-sm px-1 rounded-sm !font-mono bg-orange-400/10 text-orange-500 dark:bg-orange-300/10 dark:text-orange-300">@KevinhoMorales</span>: watching from Quito and “stealing workflow ideas.” <span class="text-sm px-1 rounded-sm !font-mono bg-orange-400/10 text-orange-500 dark:bg-orange-300/10 dark:text-orange-300">@CryptoFridge</span>: “watching this instead of another ‘AI will replace you’ thread.” <span class="text-sm px-1 rounded-sm !font-mono bg-orange-400/10 text-orange-500 dark:bg-orange-300/10 dark:text-orange-300">@corbin_braun</span>: “we need cursor back online.” <span class="text-sm px-1 rounded-sm !font-mono bg-orange-400/10 text-orange-500 dark:bg-orange-300/10 dark:text-orange-300">@taycaldwell</span> (X Developer Platform) amplified the Day 3 link. <span class="text-sm px-1 rounded-sm !font-mono bg-orange-400/10 text-orange-500 dark:bg-orange-300/10 dark:text-orange-300">@Grok</span> noted the team had pivoted toward **Cupcake** (bot-template fighter game) after an earlier food-popup idea, under the parent name **Ship by Thursday**.
